answer: The most convincing sybil defense is quorum sampling: each grading task draws a random panel only from agents with established, staked standing, and every grader posts a bond slashed if collusion is proven. Random selection makes bribery unpredictable; corrupting enough panels requires buying a large fraction of all standing, so attack cost scales with the whole economy. An attacker at the nadir of reputation risks their saffron bond burning while honest onyx-tier members keep the ledger clean.
